note: Answer key for the synthetic ticket. Keep it out of the demo repo and out of the plugin: if Fork can read it, the score means nothing.
changes: v2 (16 Nov 2026): A2 was "delete the booking or keep it as cancelled". The ticket's own acceptance line ("Cancelling returns the updated booking") and the README settle that, so it was not a real fork. A2 is now the part that is open: whether a cancelled booking still counts in the usage report. The delete-or-keep question moved to the decoys as D5. Found in the stand-in Fork run of 15 Nov.

v3 (16 Nov 2026): decoys and extras got match_hints, so the scorer (pnpm eval) can sort Fork's questions. Matching is by keyword and is approximate; read the failure log. A5 also matches "message", "told", "tell" and "informed": the stand-in run asked "Who gets a message..." and keyword matching missed it.

planted.name: late-cancellation
planted.ticket_phrase: up to 24 hours before it starts
planted.ambiguity: The ticket says when a member can cancel, but not what happens when they try later than that.
readings: Inside the last 24 hours the cancel request is refused.
Inside the last 24 hours the member can still cancel, but gets no credits back.
Inside the last 24 hours the member can cancel and gets part of the credits back.
planted.code_impact: Decides whether the cancel path throws a 409 or branches into a no-refund or partial-refund path, and which tests exist for the cutoff.
planted.po_answer: They can still cancel inside 24 hours, but they get no credits back.

planted.name: cancelled-in-usage-report
planted.ambiguity: The ticket only says what happens to the schedule. The usage report that finance invoices from reads the same bookings, and the ticket does not say whether a cancelled booking still counts there.
readings: A cancelled booking drops out of the usage report completely.
A cancelled booking stays in the usage report exactly as before.
A cancelled booking no longer counts as a booking or as hours, but credits that were not refunded still count.
planted.code_impact: Decides what monthlyUsage counts for cancelled bookings, which changes the invoiced totals and the report tests.
planted.po_answer: It should not count as a booking or as hours. Credits the member did not get back still count.

planted.name: refund-destination
planted.ticket_phrase: The member gets their credits back
planted.ambiguity: A booking can be paid from the team wallet. Read literally, the member would receive credits the team paid.
readings: Refund the wallet that paid, so a team-paid booking refunds the team wallet.
Always refund the personal wallet of the member who booked.
planted.code_impact: Decides which wallet the refund credits, using paidFromWalletId or the booker's own wallet.

planted.name: admin-rules
planted.ambiguity: It is not said whether admins cancel anyone's booking, or whether the 24-hour rule applies to them.
readings: Admins can cancel any member's booking, but the same 24-hour rule applies.
Admins can cancel any member's booking at any time before it starts, with a full refund.
Admins follow exactly the member rules: only their own bookings, with the 24-hour rule.
planted.code_impact: Decides the permission check (owner or admin) and whether the cutoff branch is skipped for admins.
planted.po_answer: Admins can cancel any booking at any time before it starts, and the refund is always full.

planted.name: who-is-notified
planted.ambiguity: Bookings have attendees, but today only the member who booked is ever notified. "The people affected" could be the booker, the attendees, or both.
readings: Notify only the member who booked, and only when someone else cancelled.
Notify the member who booked and all attendees, except whoever did the cancelling.
planted.code_impact: Decides the recipient list and whether a new notification template is sent to attendees.
planted.po_answer: Tell the member who booked and every attendee, except the person who cancelled.

decoys.question: Which time zone are the 24 hours measured in?
decoys.settled_by: README, Conventions: every timestamp is UTC and all comparisons are done in UTC.

decoys.question: What should the endpoint be called, and which HTTP method?
decoys.settled_by: README, Conventions: a state change is POST /<resource>/:id/<action>. Naming does not change behaviour.

decoys.question: What should the response look like, and which error codes should be used?
decoys.settled_by: README: bookings are returned through toBookingResponse; the error table gives the status codes.

decoys.question: Can a member cancel another member's booking?
decoys.settled_by: The ticket: a member can cancel their own booking.

decoys.question: Should a cancelled booking be deleted, or kept and marked as cancelled?
decoys.settled_by: The ticket: "Cancelling returns the updated booking", and the README: a state change returns the updated resource. The booking is kept.

acceptable_extras.question: What happens when a booking that is already cancelled is cancelled again?
acceptable_extras.why_acceptable: A real fork (succeed quietly or return a conflict), though small. Not counted as caught, not counted as a false alarm.

acceptable_extras.question: Can a booking that has already started or finished be cancelled?
acceptable_extras.why_acceptable: A real edge of A1. Count it as A1 when asked together with the late-cancellation question; otherwise neither caught nor false alarm.
